title: Two-qutrit entanglement invisible to real witnesses under every local filter
shortTitle: Real witnesses miss some two-qutrit entanglement, whatever the local filter
oneLine: An explicit two-qutrit state is detected by a complex entanglement witness but by no real witness after any local filters, disproving both parts of a 2025 conjecture.
abstract: An entanglement witness is an observable whose expectation is never negative on separable states, so a negative value certifies entanglement. Shen, Chen and Bian (Physical Review A, 2025, Conjecture 9) conjectured that real witnesses lose nothing once each party may first apply a local unitary (part i) or, more weakly, an invertible local filter (part ii). This candidate shows that both parts are false. For two qutrits, an explicit full-rank PPT entangled state, built from a separable state and an exposed witness due to Ha and Kye with epsilon = 1/160000, has expectation −8/19199997 on that complex witness, while every filtered real block-positive operator, and every limit of such operators, has expectation above 8.5×10⁻¹⁰ on it; the same holds on a Frobenius ball of radius 8×10⁻¹⁰. Part (i) already fails for a qubit paired with a four-level system (2×4, total dimension eight), the smallest possible size; whether part (ii) fails there is open. In every dimension the conjecture holds exactly when every exposed point of the set of trace-one block-positive operators is a limit of filtered real ones, and when it fails it fails for an open set of states. A degree-nine polynomial invariant decides which members of the exposed Ha–Kye family have filtered real versions, and one extra local qubit restores detection. The witness and the separable state are Ha and Kye's. Limits: the explicit state is far too close to separable for an experiment (noise threshold about 1.6×10⁻⁷), and the result concerns a single witness matrix, not measurement schemes with classical post-processing. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 12-page paper with a plain introduction (the problem, why it matters, the conjecture, what was known, what is new and a roadmap) and written proofs of every result. Five Python programs accompany it: verify_witness.py (SymPy) rebuilds the witness and separable state from Ha and Kye's data and checks the positivity conditions, spectra, Gram certificate, invariants, every constant of the bounds section and the exact state file (120 exact checks); verify_chirality.py expands the degree-nine identity and independent_tensor_check.py confirms it by modular arithmetic; verify_qubit_ququart.py rebuilds the 2×4 map and checks tr([X,Y]³) = −840i with a real control; check_block_positivity.py is a floating-point cross-check of the cited block-positivity theorems, not a proof. A clean replay reproduced every recorded output byte for byte, also under Python's optimised mode; a changed epsilon makes the main check fail; Linux CI reruns everything under a declared comparison policy. The computations accompany the written proofs; they do not replace them.

keyResults: Theorem 8 (proof, exact constants): with epsilon = 1/160000 the two-qutrit state rho_epsilon = (D − epsilon I)/(360 − 9 epsilon) is full-rank, PPT and entangled with tr(W rho_epsilon) = −8/19199997, while every filtered real block-positive operator and every limit of such operators has expectation above 8.5×10⁻¹⁰ on it, also on the Frobenius ball of radius 8×10⁻¹⁰; both parts of Shen–Chen–Bian Conjecture 9 fail for two qutrits.

Theorem 10 (proof): on C²⊗C⁴ a filtered real exposed witness lies outside the closure of the locally unitary real witnesses, since tr([X,Y]³) = −840i for its partial traces; part (i) fails in total dimension eight, the minimum. Part (ii) for 2×4 remains open.

Theorem 6 (proof): in every dimension the conjecture (either part) holds exactly when every exposed point of the trace-one block-positive operators lies in the corresponding closed real class; when it fails, the missed states include an open set of full-rank PPT states.

Lemma 7 and Theorem 9 (proof): the invariant chi(X) = Im tr M(X)³ scales by |det K|⁶ under local filters and vanishes on filtered real matrices; a degree-nine invariant decides exactly which members of the exposed Ha–Kye family have filtered real or locally unitary real versions.
Proposition 11 (proof): one extra local qubit restores detection by a real witness; a second copy of the state can act as that qubit when filters are allowed.

Credit and limits: the witness W and separable state D are Ha and Kye's, with block positivity and exposedness from their 2012 and 2013 theorems. The explicit state is far too close to separable for an experiment (noise threshold about 1.6×10⁻⁷).

narration:
To show that two quantum particles are entangled, experimenters measure an entanglement witness. Its average can only go negative when the particles really are entangled, so a negative reading is proof. A witness is written as a table of numbers, and in general those numbers are complex. Real numbers are simpler, and a natural hope is that nothing is lost by using only real tables, as long as each laboratory may first choose a good local basis, or apply a local filter that reshapes its own particle's state.

Shen, Chen and Bian conjectured exactly this, in two forms: one allowing only changes of basis, and one also allowing local filters. They proved it for many states, and it holds automatically for the smallest systems.

This release shows that both forms are false. It writes down an explicit state of two three-level systems that a complex witness detects, while every real witness misses it, whatever local filter is applied first. The same holds for every state close enough to it. The basis-change form already fails for a qubit paired with a four-level system, the smallest size where it could fail. The paper also gives a rule for every size: the conjecture holds exactly when every corner of the set of witnesses can be approached by filtered real ones. And one extra local qubit is enough to restore detection.

The idea is to take a witness that touches the unentangled states at a single point. Nudge that point slightly towards entanglement, and the witness detects the result while every filtered real witness misses it. To show that this witness is not secretly real, the paper uses a polynomial that local filters can only rescale by a positive factor, and that stays real for real tables. For this witness, the polynomial is not real, so the witness lies outside the real class.

There are limits. The explicit state sits extremely close to the unentangled ones, so this is a mathematical statement about which measurements suffice, not a proposal for an experiment. The witness and the unentangled state come from earlier work by Ha and Kye. Whether the filter form also fails for a qubit with a four-level system is still open. Experiments can still detect such states by combining several real measurements with classical processing.

This is an unrefereed candidate, checked by internal AI-assisted review and exact computer checks rather than by outside experts, so treat its conclusions as promising but provisional.
